title: SyncClock
description: common.sync-clock@1: one timeline for many players (seven domains plan B4). The authority stamps at_ms and seq when it accepts a change and fans the state out; a player computes where it should be as position_ms + (authority time now - at_ms) * rate when paused is false, and exactly position_ms when paused is true. Chat hosts a room's clock on its room socket, keeps the latest state in memory and in the room_sync_clocks table, refuses a set from anyone but the current common.control-lease@1 holder, and sends the state to a member when they join the room. Clock offset is measured over the same socket with time ping/pong pairs, best of five samples, refreshed every 60 s.

room.description: The authority's room id (Chat: the room's slug).

media.description: What is playing: an OpenVibe media ref or an https URL. A ref names a Media object; a URL is the media file itself.

position_ms.description: The media position at at_ms, in milliseconds. At most 30 days.

rate.description: The playback rate the room is playing at (1 is normal speed).

paused.description: When true the timeline stands still at position_ms; when false it advances at rate.

at_ms.description: The authority's epoch milliseconds when it accepted this state. A player subtracts this from the authority's clock now, so the value is never the player's own clock.

set_by.description: The subject that made the change (the lease holder's subject as the authority knows it).

seq.description: The timeline version: starts at 1 and increments on every accepted change. A client ignores a state with a seq it has already seen.
